slides.0.title: Geography, climate and wine regions
slides.0.subtitle: The Danube, the Pannonian climate and regional structure
slides.1.title: Location and scale
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Location
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Wine regions lie roughly between 47° and 48° N, concentrated in the east of the country
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Vineyard area
slides.1.highlights.1.content: About 44,210 ha (2024/2025 data), almost all in the east
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Area by state (2024)
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Niederösterreich about 26,700 ha, Burgenland about 11,500, Steiermark about 5,100, Wien about 600, and the other states about 240 combined
slides.1.highlights.3.title: A capital with vineyards
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Wien is one of the few capitals with sizeable vineyards inside the city
slides.1.content: Remember the order: Niederösterreich is largest, Burgenland second, Steiermark third.
slides.2.title: Climate: continental and Pannonian
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Continental-Pannonian climate
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Cold winters, hot dry summers and a long growing cycle; about 400 mm of rain in the east and up to about 800 mm in Steiermark (wein.plus)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The Danube's influence
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The river valley tempers cold Alpine winds and creates cool nights and warm days, helping retain acidity and aroma
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Neusiedler See
slides.2.highlights.2.content: A shallow steppe lake whose autumn mists and humidity make noble rot reliable most years, the basis of the sweet wines
slides.2.highlights.3.title: The warm, humid south-east
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Steiermark has warm days, cool nights and a long season, but warmth and humidity make viticulture harder
slides.2.content: The core idea: cool nights, warm days and a long season give ripeness with retained acidity.
slides.3.title: Regional structure and DACs
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Three wine-growing regions
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Weinland (Niederösterreich, Burgenland and Wien), Steirerland (Steiermark) and Bergland (the other states, with tiny areas); some sources list Wien separately
slides.3.highlights.1.title: 18 DACs
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Burgenland 6, Niederösterreich 8, Wien 1 and Steiermark 3: 18 in total (wein.plus, Wikipedia; see Level 2)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: What a DAC is
slides.3.highlights.2.content: A DAC is an appellation defined by the typical style of a region, with its rules proposed by the regional wine committee
slides.3.content: Sources count the regions differently, so the number of regions is kept out of the quiz.
slides.4.title: Terrain and soils
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Wachau terraces
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Steep terraced vineyards, with the Danube valley moderating cold Alpine winds
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Kamptal sandstone slopes
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Steep, sun-exposed sandstone slopes where Riesling excels
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Volcanic soils in south-east Steiermark
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Extinct volcanoes give rich soils, and cooler nights extend the growing season
slides.4.content: Level 2 covers soils and terrain region by region; here the goal is an impression of diversity.
Which Austrian state has the largest vineyard area?
Niederösterreich has about 26,700 ha, far more than any other state.
Which best describes the climate of Austria's main wine regions?
A. Mediterranean, mild winters and dry summers
D. Continental-Pannonian, cold winters and hot summers
Cold winters, hot dry summers and a long growing season are its hallmarks.
What happens reliably around Neusiedler See, underpinning the sweet wines?
The shallow lake's mists and humidity make noble rot likely.
